uchitpur-haor.desc: At Uchitpur in Madan upazila the road ends at the edge of a huge haor. In the monsoon the water stretches to the horizon, and the sandy banks and shallow edges give it a beach-like feel, so crowds of day-trippers come on holidays. Engine boats take visitors out across the water toward Khaliajuri and the villages that become islands in the rains. In the dry season the water draws back and the land turns into rice fields.
blocks: How to get there
From Netrokona town take a CNG or bus to Madan, then on to Uchitpur bazar and ghat (around an hour in all).
Good to know
Wear a life jacket on boats and check the weather; storms build quickly over the haor. Agree on boat fares before you set off.

birisiri-wangala.desc: Wangala is the post-harvest festival of the Garo people, offering thanks to Saljong, the sun god, for the year's crops. In Birisiri and nearby villages it is celebrated in late autumn with drumming, traditional dress and group dances. Rice, rice beer and the first fruits of the harvest are part of the rituals. Visitors who come with a local contact are usually welcome to watch.
blocks: Good to know
Ask before photographing and follow the hosts' lead.

glance: 150 km to Netrokona by road, 4–5 hours by bus or car
chandradinga-hill.desc: Chandradinga is a hill in Kalmakanda upazila, part of the Garo Hills that spill over from Meghalaya. Its outline looks like an upturned boat, and locals link it to the Manasamangal story in which the goddess Manasa sank the seven boats of the merchant Chand Sadagar; a group of rocks here are said to be those boats. From the top there are wide views over the border hills and the plains. A small waterfall at nearby Panchgaon village is part of the same outing.
blocks: How to get there
From Netrokona town take a bus or CNG to Kalmakanda, then a motorbike or CNG toward Panchgaon near the border.
Good to know
This is a border area; carry your NID or passport and don't go past BGB posts. Roads and toilets are basic, so plan for that.

glance: 150 km to Netrokona by road, 4–5 hours by bus or car
dingapota-haor.desc: Dingapota Haor in Mohanganj upazila is one of Netrokona's largest haors. In the rainy season it spreads into a wide sheet of water, with village islands, hijal trees standing in the water and fishermen casting nets. In winter the water recedes and the land turns into paddy fields and grazing for duck flocks. Boat trips from Mohanganj are the best way to see it.
blocks: How to get there
Train or bus from Mymensingh or Netrokona to Mohanganj, then hire a boat at the haor ghat.
Good to know
Use boats with life jackets and avoid storms, which can come up fast.

netrokona-baul-songs.desc: Netrokona has produced some of Bengal's best-loved folk and mystic poets, including Jalal Uddin Khan of Kendua and Ukil Munshi of Khaliajuri. Their songs explore love, the body and the search for the divine, and are still sung by village singers and on national stages. Night-long song gatherings and fairs, especially in winter, keep the tradition alive. Ask locally about upcoming performances.

netrokona-balish-misti.desc: Balish misti takes its name from its shape: a large, plump sweet that looks like a little pillow. It is made from chhana and flour, fried, soaked in syrup and finished with a layer of thick khir. The sweet was created by Gayanath Ghosh's shop in Netrokona town, and the shop is still the place most people seek out. One piece is enough for two.

bijoypur-china-clay-hills.desc: At Bijoypur near Durgapur, low hills are made of white kaolin (china clay) mined for ceramics. Years of digging have left terraced slopes of white, cream and pinkish clay beside pools of turquoise and green water. The contrast with the green hills and the sky makes it one of the most photographed landscapes in northern Bangladesh. Paths can be slippery, especially after rain.
blocks: How to get there
From Birisiri cross the Someshwari by ferry or boat, then take an auto or motorbike to Bijoypur.
Good to know
Stay away from active mining edges and do not swim in the pits.

glance: 150 km to Netrokona by road, 4–5 hours by bus or car
birisiri-someshwari.desc: Birisiri, in Durgapur upazila, is the gateway to Netrokona's hill country. The Someshwari river comes down from Meghalaya with clear water over wide sand and stone beds, and in winter you can walk across parts of it. Sand and coal boats work the river, and the blue hills of India rise just beyond. The Birisiri Cultural Academy introduces the Garo, Hajong and other local peoples.
blocks: How to get there
Bus from Dhaka (Mohakhali) to Durgapur/Birisiri, about 5–6 hours; or via Netrokona town by bus or CNG.
Good to know
Stay overnight in Birisiri; hire an auto or motorbike for the china-clay hills and border areas.

ranikhong-mission.desc: Ranikhong Mission, founded in the early 20th century, stands on a small hill near the Someshwari in Durgapur upazila. Its church and school serve the local Garo Christian community. From the hilltop you look out over the river, the sandbanks and the Meghalaya hills. It is a peaceful place, especially in early morning.
blocks: How to get there
From Birisiri take an auto or motorbike towards Ranikhong, about 20–30 minutes.
Good to know
It is an active religious site; dress modestly and be quiet during services.

glance: 150 km to Netrokona by road, 4–5 hours by bus or car
roailbari-fort.desc: Roailbari, also called Kotbari fort, lies on the bank of the Betai river about 13 km south-west of Kendua upazila town. It is a group of old structures rather than a single building, and today only roofless walls and the outlines of the buildings remain. It is one of the archaeological sites of the district, but few travellers ever find their way here, so expect a village setting and no facilities.
blocks: How to get there
From Netrokona take a bus or CNG to Kendua, then a CNG or auto to Roailbari Amtala union.
Good to know
Ask locals to guide you to the ruins. Don't climb on the old walls.

saat-shahid-mazar-lengura.desc: On 26 July 1971 seven freedom fighters were killed fighting the Pakistani army near the Nazirpur union land office in Kalmakanda. They were buried at Fulbari in Lengura union, at the foot of the hills on the border, and the site is now known as Saat Shahid Mazar or Saptashikha. It is a quiet, green spot in the same hilly border country as Chandradinga, and local visitors come both to pay respects and to enjoy the view of the hills.
blocks: How to get there
From Kalmakanda upazila town take a motorbike or CNG to Lengura and Fulbari.
Good to know
It is a grave site; keep voices low and don't climb on the memorial. Carry ID in this border area.

netrokona-haor-fish.desc: The haors of southern Netrokona are rich in freshwater fish such as boal, ayre, rui and countless small species. As the water drops in late autumn and winter, fishermen catch large numbers of small fish and dry them on bamboo racks as shutki. Locals cook shutki bhorta, a fiery mash, and fresh fish in light curries. The bazaars of Mohanganj and Khaliajuri are the place to sample them.
